clue.text: New rise accepted by TV presenter -a border dweller

indicators.note: something accepted by a person is taken in, so the shuffled letters go inside the presenter

parts.note: a frontman is the presenter who fronts a television show

indicators.note: new here means remade, so the letters of rise are put in a fresh order

explanation.surface: A fresh rise in pay is taken by a television host who lives near the border.
explanation.walkthrough: 'New' rearranges the letters of the word rise, and 'accepted by' puts them inside the presenter.
explanation.definitionFit: A frontiersman lives on the frontier, the borderland at the edge of settled country.

clue.text: Odd telly characters upholding trees before all else

indicators.note: in a down clue the piece that upholds sits below, so the odd letters come after the trees

parts.note: firs are coniferous trees

indicators.note: the odd characters are the first, third and fifth letters of telly

explanation.surface: Strange television personalities hold up some trees before anything else.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Odd' picks T, L, Y from TELLY; 'upholding' sets them beneath FIRS in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: Firstly introduces the point that comes ahead of every other one.

clue.text: Rock is broadcast live on One

indicators.note: broadcast means scattered about, so the letters of live, on and the I are strewn into a new order

parts.note: one is I, the Roman numeral

explanation.surface: A rock band plays live on BBC One.
explanation.walkthrough: 'broadcast' scatters LIVE, ON and I (one) into the answer; 'is' just links.
explanation.definitionFit: Olivine is a green silicate mineral found in volcanic rock such as basalt.

clue.text: Sensational article about King Dicky?

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the article wraps round the king and the sickly piece

parts.note: an article is a thing, an object
R is short for Rex, Latin for king
dicky is British slang for weak or unwell, as in a dicky heart

explanation.surface: A tabloid piece about Richard the king, nicknamed Dicky.
explanation.walkthrough: The article is not 'the' or 'a' but an object. Dicky is British slang for poorly.
explanation.definitionFit: Something thrilling is exciting, causing a sensation.

clue.text: Follow directions and prefer charges

parts.note: E and N are compass points, east and north
to prefer charges against someone is to sue them, bringing a case

explanation.surface: Someone is told to follow instructions and take a matter to court.
explanation.definitionFit: To ensue is to come after as a result, i.e. to succeed in sequence.

clue.text: Male worker in confines of suburban liquor-house

indicators.note: in means the man and the worker are placed inside the edges of suburban
the confines of a word are its boundaries, its first and last letters

parts.note: he is the male pronoun
a worker bee is the crossword's standard worker

explanation.surface: A man who works within the limits of a suburb runs a drinking den.
explanation.walkthrough: 'confines of' gives S and N, the first and last letters of 'suburban'. A shebeen is an Irish or Scottish illicit bar.
explanation.definitionFit: A shebeen is an unlicensed drinking establishment, a place selling liquor illegally.

clue.text: Publicity about ship on river makes us confident

indicators.note: about means going around, so the advert surrounds the ship and river

parts.note: an ad is a piece of publicity
SS stands for steamship
the Ure is a river in Yorkshire

explanation.surface: An advert about a ship on a river reassures us.
explanation.walkthrough: AD goes 'about' SS placed on URE, a Yorkshire river; 'makes us' links to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Assured means self-possessed and sure of oneself.

clue.text: Marksman notes owl, for example

parts.note: sharps are musical notes raised a semitone
an owl is a hooter, one example of a bird that hoots

explanation.surface: A sniper takes note of an owl.
explanation.definitionFit: A sharpshooter is an expert shot, someone skilled with a rifle.

clue.text: He causes vexation to a cross-country runner

explanation.surface: Someone annoys a person who runs across fields.
explanation.definitionFit: One who harries others torments them; a harrier is also a runner in cross-country races, named from hounds.

clue.text: Measures supported by David Copperfield, relatively speaking

parts.note: steps are measures, as in taking steps to deal with something
something supported by another sits on it

explanation.surface: Measures are backed by the novel's hero, speaking of his family.
explanation.walkthrough: In Dickens's novel David Copperfield's mother marries Mr Murdstone, making David his stepson.
explanation.definitionFit: David becomes Murdstone's stepson, a child by marriage rather than by blood.

clue.text: Statesman's den and green lawn, possibly?

indicators.note: possibly signals a rearrangement, one possible ordering of the letters of den, green and lawn

explanation.surface: A politician's study and his green garden lawn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'possibly' rearranges DEN, GREEN and LAWN; 'and' only joins. 'Statesman's' reads as 'Statesman is': a man from one of the six New England States.
explanation.definitionFit: A New Englander comes from one of the north-eastern US states, so is a state's man.

clue.text: Hearing again about a pain in the neck

parts.note: re means about or concerning
a trial is a nuisance, something trying

explanation.surface: Someone is told again about a stiff neck.
explanation.definitionFit: A retrial is a case heard a second time in court.

clue.text: Cockney intellectual, by the sound of it, in "Hair'"?

indicators.note: a Cockney speaker drops the initial h, so the word is said without it
by the sound of it says the word is judged by how it is pronounced

parts.note: a highbrow is an intellectual

explanation.surface: A clever Londoner appears in the musical Hair.
explanation.walkthrough: Cockney Londoners drop the H, so 'ighbrow sounds like the answer. 'Hair' is in quotation marks, as if the musical.
explanation.definitionFit: The arch of hair above each eye is the brow's own growth.

clue.text: Type of writing instrument

explanation.surface: Someone asks what kind of pen this is.
explanation.definitionFit: Style means a kind or manner; a style is also a stylus, a pointed tool for writing on wax.

clue.text: Extinct reptile's droppings found in island river

indicators.note: found in means the droppings sit inside the island and river pair

parts.note: the Don is a river in England and Scotland
guano is seabird or bat droppings

explanation.surface: Dung from a prehistoric creature is discovered on an island river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reptile's' reads as 'reptile is'. GUANO is 'found in' I DON.
explanation.definitionFit: The iguanodon was a large plant-eating dinosaur, long extinct.

clue.text: Powerless to contain the net rise — it's indefensible

indicators.note: to contain means to hold inside, so powerless wraps the turned net

parts.note: unable means powerless to do something

indicators.note: in a down clue rise means the word net reads upwards

explanation.surface: A goalkeeper is helpless as the ball rises into the net; the defence collapses.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rise' reads 'net' upwards in this down entry; 'the' and 'it's' only link.
explanation.definitionFit: An untenable position cannot be held or defended.

clue.text: About to scream in street attack

parts.note: on means about, as in a talk on a subject

indicators.note: in places the scream inside the street abbreviation

parts.note: a scream is something hilarious, a laugh

explanation.surface: Someone is on the point of screaming as a street assault happens.
explanation.walkthrough: 'scream' is a noun here, meaning a hilarious thing, not a shout; 'to' only links.
explanation.definitionFit: An onslaught is a fierce assault.

clue.text: Upset priest's son — one over a European territory

indicators.note: upset in a down clue turns the priest's name upside down

parts.note: Eli is the priest in the Book of Samuel, so priest's gives Eli's
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A clergyman's son is upset that someone has been put above a whole region.
explanation.walkthrough: Eli is the priest who raised Samuel; 'Upset' turns his possessive upwards in the down entry, and 'over' puts the one above A.
explanation.definitionFit: Silesia is a historical region of central Europe, now mostly in Poland.

clue.text: Like the surroundings of man? I bet it's otherwise

indicators.note: otherwise means arranged differently, so the letters of man and I bet are reordered

explanation.surface: Someone muses on a man's environment, betting it is not as it seems.
explanation.walkthrough: 'otherwise' rearranges MAN and I BET.
explanation.definitionFit: Ambient describes the surrounding environment, such as ambient temperature.

clue.text: Unqualified to teach African languages at first

indicators.note: at first takes the opening letter of each of the three words before it

explanation.surface: A person without qualifications sets out to teach African languages.
explanation.walkthrough: TO plus T, A, L, the first letters of 'teach African languages'.
explanation.definitionFit: Total means complete, without reservation, as in total nonsense.

clue.text: Flyer also seen around posh car club

indicators.note: seen around means the word for also is wrapped round the other pieces

parts.note: too means also
U means upper-class, posh
the RAC is the Royal Automobile Club

explanation.surface: A bird is also spotted near a smart motoring club.
explanation.walkthrough: The RAC (Royal Automobile Club) is a British motoring organisation; U is old slang for upper-class.
explanation.definitionFit: A touraco is a colourful African bird, and birds fly.

clue.text: Pushes one out of this, replacing it with a red coat

indicators.note: one out of this means the I is taken away from the word this
replacing it with puts the new piece where the I was

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one
rust is a reddish coating that forms on iron

explanation.surface: Someone forces a soldier out, putting a redcoat in his place.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out of' removes I (one) from THIS and 'replacing it with' puts RUST, a red coating, in its place.
explanation.definitionFit: Thrusts means shoves forcefully.

clue.text: Where travellers pay to ring the pub?

parts.note: to toll is to ring a bell slowly
a bar is a pub

explanation.surface: Drivers pay to phone the local pub.
explanation.definitionFit: A toll-bar is the barrier on a road where a toll must be paid to pass.

clue.text: Turpentine product from Patros, indispensable to those on the fiddle

indicators.note: from signals that the letters are taken out of the words Patros, indispensable

explanation.surface: A substance from the Greek port of Patros is essential to violinists.
explanation.walkthrough: The run sits 'from' patROS INdispensable. The rest of the clue adds that violinists rub it on their bows.
explanation.definitionFit: Rosin is the resin left after distilling turpentine, used on string players' bows.

clue.text: Turn one out, though it's a little matter and there's no charge

definitions.text: a little matter and there's no charge

indicators.note: out means put out of order, so the letters of turn one are shuffled

explanation.surface: Someone shrugs off a small matter since it costs nothing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' rearranges TURN ONE; 'though it's' links.
explanation.definitionFit: This subatomic particle is a tiny piece of matter carrying no electric charge.

clue.text: Bacon's more adventurous son

parts.note: rasher, an old comparative of rash, means more reckless

explanation.surface: The philosopher Bacon had a bolder son.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bacon's' reads as 'Bacon is', with Francis Bacon as the decoy.
explanation.definitionFit: Rashers are slices of bacon.

clue.text: Club supporter not about

indicators.note: not means the piece for about is left out

parts.note: a brassiere supports the bust
re means about

explanation.surface: A fan of a club stays away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not' takes RE (about) out of BRASSIERE. A brassie is an old wooden golf club, the two wood.
explanation.definitionFit: A brassie was a golf wood with a brass sole plate.

clue.text: Bad-tempered when two vessels start to overtake us

parts.note: a can is a vessel for holding liquid
a tanker is a vessel, a ship carrying oil

indicators.note: start to means the opening letter of overtake

explanation.surface: A driver gets irritable when two ships begin to pass.
explanation.walkthrough: CAN and TANKER are the two vessels, then O from 'start to overtake' and US.
explanation.definitionFit: Cantankerous means irritable and quarrelsome.
